limitations.limitation: MSE, MAE, PSNR, and SSIM quantify numerical similarity to the known clean reference. They do not directly measure historical plausibility, artistic appropriateness, semantic correctness, or conservation acceptability.
limitations.implication: The metrics must be interpreted alongside perceptual, semantic, texture, uncertainty, and visual analyses in later notebooks.

limitations.limitation: Masked-region MSE, MAE, and PSNR treat all selected pixels equally and ignore spatial arrangement.
limitations.implication: Strong masked-region error reduction does not prove that reconstructed structures or brushwork are visually convincing.

limitations.limitation: SSIM requires contiguous spatial structure and is therefore not computed over irregular masked, boundary, or outside-mask pixel selections.
limitations.implication: SSIM comparisons are restricted to full-image, content-region, and mask-bounding-box crops.

limitations.limitation: The mask bounding-box crop includes unmasked context around the damaged region and may therefore dilute or stabilize the measured restoration effect.
limitations.implication: Bounding-box metrics should be interpreted together with masked-region and boundary-region metrics.

limitations.limitation: The boundary region is defined algorithmically using a morphological band of 5 pixels.
limitations.implication: Boundary scores depend partly on this chosen width and will later be complemented by dedicated seam and color-consistency analysis.

limitations.limitation: Outside-mask metrics are dominated by the large unchanged image area and may hide small unintended changes near the restoration boundary.
limitations.implication: Outside-mask metrics are diagnostic controls rather than primary restoration-quality measures.

limitations.limitation: Zero-control cases contain no missing-content target and therefore do not support masked, bounding-box, or boundary-region evaluation.
limitations.implication: They are used to test whether the restoration pipeline unnecessarily alters intact images.

limitations.limitation: Synthetic-degradation masks represent grayscale effect intensity rather than ordinary binary missing-content masks. The evaluation target is thresholded using intensity > 127.
limitations.implication: Synthetic-degradation results remain supplementary and should not be pooled uncritically with primary missing-content experiments.

limitations.limitation: This notebook evaluates only OpenCV Telea outputs.
limitations.implication: Cross-model conclusions require equivalent metric computation for LaMa, Stable Diffusion, SDXL, and other restoration methods.
